section_summary: This section concludes a general guide to private foreign trade in occupied Japan and reproduces SCAP Circular No. 3, which regulated the admission, conduct, travel, finances, and logistical support of private commercial entrants. The remainder consists chiefly of State, Commerce, Army, embassy, and consular correspondence concerning individual entry permits, applicant lists, travel documentation, visa or exit-permit waivers, and repatriation. Smaller groups concern the Tacla family’s proposed journey to Brazil, Japanese repatriation from Chile, and Philippine import documentation.

subfiles.title: Private Trade in Japan: Shipping, Claims, Insurance, and Eligibility (conclusion)
subfiles.about: Concludes instructions governing shipping, claims, insurance, and participation in Japan’s private foreign trade.
subfiles.summary: Lists authorized steamship agencies and explains shipping documents, claims, foreign insurance, and eligibility for private trade. Foreign residents could trade through Boeki Cho, while permanent agency arrangements required SCAP approval.

subfiles.title: SCAP Circular No. 3: Private Commercial Entrants
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: Occupation authorities and prospective commercial entrants
subfiles.about: Establishes comprehensive rules for private commercial entrants traveling to and operating in occupied Japan.
subfiles.summary: The circular defines eligible commercial purposes and prescribes sponsorship, application data, entry documents, health requirements, registration, identification cards, and travel authorization. It regulates residence permits, legal jurisdiction, taxation, currency, trade through Boeki Cho, accommodations, transportation, communications, and medical services. It also assigns administrative responsibilities to SCAP and the Eighth Army and restricts dependents, automobiles, postal access, military facilities, and private trading by occupation personnel.

subfiles.title: Department of State Charge Slip, File 894.111/6-748
subfiles.about: Records the internal charging and later return of papers from the decimal file.
subfiles.summary: Internal charge slip recording circulation and return of file papers.

subfiles.title: Authorization for Hilton S. Pedley to Enter Japan
subfiles.about: Authorizes Hilton S. Pedley’s business entry into Japan for a sixty-day stay.
subfiles.summary: Directs Manila to document Pedley’s military clearance and advise him to carry two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Transmission of South African Applications to the Army
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Department of State
subfiles.to: Lieutenant Colonel J. D. Scott, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Forwards four applications covering five South Africans for SCAP consideration.
subfiles.summary: Requests Army submission of the Patel, de Villiers, Simson, and Lachman applications to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Authorization for Natalio M. Balboa to Enter Japan
subfiles.about: Notifies Manila that Natalio M. Balboa may visit Japan for three weeks.
subfiles.summary: Reports Balboa’s clearance and Philippine delegation support, with instructions concerning photographs and entry documentation.

subfiles.title: Army Clearance for Natalio M. Balboa
subfiles.from: J. D. Scott, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Reports theater clearance for Natalio M. Balboa and requests notification of Manila.
subfiles.summary: Confirms Balboa’s three-week clearance and logistical support by the Philippine Reparations and Restitution Delegation.

subfiles.title: South African Note Transmitting H. Simson’s Application
subfiles.from: Legation of the Union of South Africa
subfiles.about: Transmits H. Simson’s sponsored application for admission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Requests notification of the result of H. Simson’s application.

subfiles.title: South African Note Transmitting Fred Lachman’s Application
subfiles.from: Legation of the Union of South Africa
subfiles.about: Transmits Fred Lachman’s sponsored application for admission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Requests notification of the result of Fred Lachman’s application.

subfiles.title: South African Note Transmitting R. C. Patel’s Application
subfiles.from: Legation of the Union of South Africa
subfiles.about: Transmits R. C. Patel’s sponsored application for admission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Requests notification of the result of R. C. Patel’s application.

subfiles.title: South African Note Transmitting the de Villiers Applications
subfiles.from: Legation of the Union of South Africa
subfiles.about: Transmits the sponsored applications of George Victor de Villiers and his wife.
subfiles.summary: Requests notification of the result of the de Villiers applications.

subfiles.title: Request to Notify Singapore of de Villiers’s Clearance
subfiles.about: Records a South African request to cable George de Villiers’s clearance to Singapore.
subfiles.summary: Mr. Botha reported de Villiers’s imminent arrival in Singapore and offered to pay for notification of the American consul.

subfiles.title: Army Notice of South African Entry Clearances
subfiles.from: Louie T. Rawls, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Reports approved entry periods for four South Africans and the withholding of Mrs. de Villiers’s permit.
subfiles.summary: Patel and George de Villiers were cleared for August entry; Simson and Lachman for mid-July to mid-August. Mrs. de Villiers’s request remained pending.

subfiles.title: Department Note Reporting South African Clearance Decisions
subfiles.to: Legation of the Union of South Africa
subfiles.about: Reports clearance dates and explains why Mrs. de Villiers’s application remained pending.
subfiles.summary: The Department confirms sixty-day visits for Simson, Lachman, Patel, and George de Villiers. It requests more information about Mrs. de Villiers’s business purpose and reviews the required passport endorsement.

subfiles.title: Commerce Department Transmittal of Approved Japan Applicants
subfiles.to: Herbert Corkran Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards a list of Commerce-approved applicants for travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Transmits approved applicants and copies of foreign nationals’ applications for final SCAP action.

subfiles.title: Applicants Approved by Commerce Department, June 3, 1948
subfiles.about: Lists firms, representatives, citizenship, requested entry dates, and transportation for proposed Japan travel.
subfiles.summary: Names Commerce-approved applicants from Honolulu, Los Angeles, New York, and San Francisco, including Victor C. Moche, whose later clearance appears in this section.

subfiles.title: Brazilian Embassy Note Concerning the Tacla Family
subfiles.about: Clarifies financing and visa conditions for Naji Tacla and his family.
subfiles.summary: Brazil disclaims responsibility for the family’s travel expenses and states that temporary visas depend on meeting its San Francisco consulate’s legal requirements.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Yokohama Concerning the Tacla Family
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, Yokohama Branch, Office of the United States Political Adviser
subfiles.about: Requests assistance and a report concerning the Tacla family’s onward journey from Japan to Brazil.
subfiles.summary: Forwards earlier correspondence and asks Yokohama to report any further action facilitating the family’s travel.

subfiles.title: Draft Reply to Brazil Concerning the Tacla Family
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Brazil’s conditions and describes an inquiry into consular requirements for the Tacla family.
subfiles.summary: The Department notes that Tacla must satisfy the Brazilian Consulate General in San Francisco. It says Yokohama has been asked to report further action regarding the journey.

subfiles.title: Telephone Inquiry to the Brazilian Embassy
subfiles.about: Records an inquiry about Brazilian visa requirements for Naji Tacla’s family.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy could not specify requirements and suggested direct correspondence with its San Francisco consulate.

subfiles.title: Commerce Department Transmittal of Japan and Korea Applicants
subfiles.to: Herbert Corkran Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards Commerce-approved applicants for travel to Japan and Korea.
subfiles.summary: Submits the attached applicant list for final SCAP approval.

subfiles.title: Applicants Approved for Japan and Korea Travel, June 14, 1948
subfiles.about: Lists commercial applicants, firms, citizenship, locations, travel dates, and transportation for Japan and Korea.
subfiles.summary: The list covers applicants from Detroit, Honolulu, Los Angeles, New York, Pittsburgh, and Washington. It includes foreign nationals in Manila and Shanghai and a separate Korea request from Irving Ross.

subfiles.title: Mexico Embassy Despatch Transmitting Circular No. 1103
subfiles.about: Transmits a circular explaining documentation requirements for Japanese nationals returning to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Forwards four copies of Circular No. 1103 for the Department’s files.

subfiles.title: Circular No. 1103: Entry of Japanese Nationals into Japan
subfiles.to: United States consular officers in Mexico
subfiles.about: States that returning Japanese nationals need no special entry documentation.
subfiles.summary: Advises consular officers that neither military-government nor Japanese regulations require special documents for returning Japanese.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Kurth O. Skulstad About Japan Travel
subfiles.about: Explains the proper application channel and exit-permit treatment for Kurth O. Skulstad.
subfiles.summary: Corkran directed Skulstad to Commerce and explained that State could waive exit-permit requirements after military clearance.

subfiles.title: Address Sheet for Skulstad Correspondence
subfiles.about: Addresses Skulstad-related correspondence to the Passport Division.
subfiles.summary: Address sheet for correspondence sent to the Passport Division.

subfiles.title: Kurth O. Skulstad’s Request for Form AD-1
subfiles.about: Requests an exit-permit form for proposed business travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Skulstad describes his Norwegian citizenship, reentry application, and proposed work on oil-tanker construction in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: State Department Reply to Kurth O. Skulstad
subfiles.about: Directs Skulstad to apply through Commerce and promises later action on his exit requirement.
subfiles.summary: Advises application through Commerce’s New York office and postpones the exit waiver until military clearance arrives.

subfiles.title: Army Request for More Information About Josef Zuna
subfiles.from: J. D. Scott, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Requests details of Josef Zuna’s transportation and proposed merchandise before resubmission to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Theater headquarters requires Zuna’s travel mode and specific proposed purchases and sales.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Josef Zuna’s Application
subfiles.to: J. D. Scott, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Forwards Josef Zuna’s business-travel application for SCAP consideration.
subfiles.summary: Requests Army transmission of the Czechoslovak shoe-company director’s application to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Czechoslovak Embassy Memorandum Transmitting Josef Zuna’s Application
subfiles.about: Transmits Josef Zuna’s application for business entry into Japan.
subfiles.summary: Requests referral of Zuna’s application to the military authorities in Japan.

subfiles.title: Envelope for the Czechoslovak Application
subfiles.about: Envelope associated with the Zuna application.
subfiles.summary: Postmarked envelope accompanying the Czechoslovak submission.

subfiles.title: Josef Zuna Application for Permission to Enter Japan
subfiles.from: Josef Zuna, through the Czechoslovak Embassy
subfiles.about: Provides Zuna’s identity, occupation, itinerary, passport, purpose, and requested entry period.
subfiles.summary: Zuna proposed a three-week August visit to Tokyo to establish trade connections, buy Japanese goods, and sell Czechoslovak products. He planned to travel from Malaya through Singapore, Bangkok, and Shanghai.

subfiles.title: Request to the Czechoslovak Embassy for More Zuna Information
subfiles.about: Requests Zuna’s travel mode and more specific information about the goods he proposed to trade.
subfiles.summary: Explains that theater headquarters needs additional transportation and commodity details before considering the application further.

subfiles.title: Manila Telegram Requesting Clearance for John M. Bowes
subfiles.about: Requests validation of John M. Bowes’s Canadian passport for a two-week business visit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Bowes sought to purchase cement, construction materials, chinaware, and toys for an American firm in the Philippines.

subfiles.title: Reply to Manila on John M. Bowes and Application Channels
subfiles.about: Reports Bowes’s application is being presented to SCAP and clarifies which government may sponsor mixed-nationality cases.
subfiles.summary: Authorizes Manila to handle applications when either the firm or employee is American.

subfiles.title: Policy on Sponsoring Mixed-Nationality Commercial Applicants
subfiles.about: Records SCAP policy when an employee and employing firm have different nationalities.
subfiles.summary: Either the employee’s or firm’s government may apply; American channels are available if either is American.

subfiles.title: Submission of John M. Bowes’s Application to the Army
subfiles.to: J. D. Scott, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Summarizes John M. Bowes’s proposed business trip and requests SCAP consideration.
subfiles.summary: Provides Bowes’s passport, birth, employer, intended purchases, itinerary, and proposed two-week stay.

subfiles.title: Siamese Acknowledgment of Lieutenant Angkasaba’s Clearance
subfiles.about: Acknowledges permission for Lieutenant Angkasaba to enter Japan and thanks the Department.
subfiles.summary: Confirms that Siam’s government was informed of the conditions attached to Angkasaba’s clearance.

subfiles.title: Military Clearance Notice for Tientsin Commercial Representatives
subfiles.about: Lists Tientsin representatives cleared to enter Japan and requests notification of the appropriate agency.
subfiles.summary: Reports July–August entry clearances for representatives including W. P. Herman, D. Roy Lus, Teresh J. Sabath, and Paul E. Sernau.

subfiles.title: Americo Guerra’s Planned Departure for Japan
subfiles.about: Records Americo Guerra’s planned June 25 departure from Los Angeles for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Notes that the Argentine citizen already held an Army military permit.

subfiles.title: Receipt for Americo Guerra’s Military Permit
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of Guerra’s permit and its restriction on exclusive private-firm relations.
subfiles.summary: Confirms receipt of Permit 1471 and acceptance of its business restriction.

subfiles.title: Action Slip for Americo Guerra’s Japan Travel
subfiles.about: Records military action on Americo Guerra’s proposed travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: States that exclusive business relations with private Japanese firms were prohibited.

subfiles.title: Visa Division Exit-Permit Waiver Record for Americo Guerra
subfiles.about: Records waiver of Americo Guerra’s exit permit for travel from Los Angeles to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Exit-permit waiver card for Guerra’s June 25 departure.

subfiles.title: Request to Waive Americo Guerra’s Exit Permit
subfiles.about: Requests waiver of exit requirements for Americo Guerra’s June 25 flight to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Asks the Visa Division to waive Guerra’s exit permit despite unavailable flight details.

subfiles.title: Alexandria Inquiry About Maurice Debotton
subfiles.about: Reports Maurice Debotton’s request to enter Japan for an Egyptian cotton–Japanese tobacco barter arrangement.
subfiles.summary: The Portuguese merchant sought SCAP permission after advice from his New York agent.

subfiles.title: Instructions to Alexandria Concerning Maurice Debotton
subfiles.about: Explains Portuguese and possible American channels for Debotton’s Japan application.
subfiles.summary: Directs Debotton toward Portuguese sponsorship while noting that an American employer could apply through Commerce.

subfiles.title: Letter to Mediterranean Merchants Concerning Maurice Debotton
subfiles.about: Explains the possible sponsorship routes for Maurice Debotton’s application.
subfiles.summary: Suggests Portuguese channels or, if the firm is American, application through Commerce’s New York regional office.

subfiles.title: Report of Hiroshi Yamada Yoshiro’s Departure from Japan
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser, Yokohama
subfiles.about: Reports that a Chilean citizen departed Yokohama for San Francisco aboard the President Wilson.
subfiles.summary: Confirms the subject’s June 4 repatriation departure and expected June 14 arrival.

subfiles.title: Philippine Requirements for Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Shipments
subfiles.about: Explains Philippine documentation requirements and waivers for imported food shipments.
subfiles.summary: Although Form FA-53 was generally required, United States inspection certificates often sufficed. Philippine customs formally waived Forms 53 and 55 for qualifying meat products, with a similar practice understood for other processed foods; grower certificates applied only to fresh produce.

subfiles.title: File Request for Baghdad Telegram No. 217
subfiles.about: Requests retrieval of Telegram No. 217 to or from Baghdad.
subfiles.summary: Records a file search for Baghdad Telegram No. 217.

subfiles.title: SCAP Clearance for Conrad Roger
subfiles.to: Department of the Army and related authorities
subfiles.about: Grants stateless refugee Conrad Roger entry into Japan for permanent residence.
subfiles.summary: Authorizes repatriation shipping from Dairen and requests vessel and arrival information.

subfiles.title: Notification of Victor C. Moche’s Theater Clearance
subfiles.about: Records notification to Ruxton Textile Mills that Victor C. Moche was cleared for July entry.
subfiles.summary: The company confirmed Moche was in Baghdad and agreed to pay for notifying the Embassy there.

subfiles.title: Military Clearance for Victor C. Moche
subfiles.about: Confirms Victor C. Moche’s clearance for Japan and records a later extension of his entry period.
subfiles.summary: Moche was cleared for July entry, with an annotation extending the permissible entry period through August 31.
